correctness.rationale: The phase normalization covers exactly q^7 representatives. Cyclotomic minimal-polynomial reduction makes zero-mean detection exact. The norm polynomial for sixth roots and quadratic integer pairs for eighth roots prove the computed correlation defect is exact and comparable without rounding. The standalone exhaustive verifier passed all four cardinalities (35, 1225, 9135, 23765), minima (16, 16, 4, 24-16 sqrt(2)), optimizer counts (12, 84, 6, 6), the six-pattern octary equality classification and its second exact energy. Fourier Parseval verifies the equivalent spectral variance normalization. No infinite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: Published conference-signal work proves exact flatness for unrestricted unimodular entries, but does not imply minimum nonzero squared autocorrelation error within the restricted integer phase alphabets on cyclic order nine. Perfect/nearly-perfect prime-ary constructions concern existence, not exact subcritical squared defects. Published nine-mode Cartesian-aperture phase moments are mathematically distinct. Targeted literature and mathematical-record searches found no equal or stronger covering claim; an unindexed earlier computation remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The nine-cycle is the first nonprime odd square cyclic group, and a punctured zero-mean conference waveform is a natural Fourier-flatness design problem. Finite q-phase alphabets model constrained phase resolution. An exact optimal least-squares conference error, not merely zero/nonzero feasibility, gives a quantitative design barrier; four natural alphabets exhibit distinct numerical optima and the precise eighth-root minimum has a complete six-pattern equality classification. Its spectral variance interpretation makes the invariant intrinsically motivated and reusable in quantized conference design.
